Build a destination-neutral display plan from a table spec

Source: R/display-plan.R
apa_display_plan.Rd

Walks an apa_table_spec once and produces a plan describing how the table should be laid out, with every destination-specific decision left to the caller. The plan is consumed by apa_latex_table() (Quarto PDF, the native LaTeX emitter) and by apa_flextable() (which now writes only Word and HTML), and will also be consumed by a pandoc-markdown emitter – so it carries only structure: column count and alignment codes, header rows (with spans and rule ranges expressed as column indices, never as \cmidrule or any other markup), and body rows. Richtext runs (see rt_run) pass through unconverted so no emitter loses italics, superscripts, or symbols; each destination-specific backend (rt_to_paragraph() for flextable, rt_run_to_ftext() for Word via officer, rt_to_markdown() for pandoc) converts them at the point of use, not here.

Usage

apa_display_plan(spec)

Arguments

spec

An apa_table_spec, or an apa.*.table() result carrying one (see as_spec).

Value

A list with elements n_col (integer), align (character vector of "l"/"r"/"c", length n_col), header, and body as described above.

Details

header is a list of rows in RENDERING order: the highest spanner level first, descending through any lower levels, with the column-label row always last. Each row is list(cells = <list of cell>, rules = <list of column ranges>). Each cell is list(rt = <richtext>, span = <columns it covers>, align = <"l"/"r"/"c">); a column not covered by any spanner at that level becomes a separate blank, span-1 cell, so a row's cell spans always sum to n_col. rules lists the column range (c(from, to)) each spanner in that row covers – the caller decides what to draw there (a \cmidrule, a bottom border, nothing).

body is a list of rows: a list(type = "group", label = <richtext>) entry appears immediately before the first data row of a row group (added by the internal apa_row_group(), which has no help page to link to), and every spec body row becomes a list(type = "data", cells = <list of richtext, one per column>) entry. A spec with no row groups produces an all-"data" body, reproducing a flat table exactly.

Every spanner's columns must be contiguous, and no two spanners at the same level may share a column; either shape makes the header-row walk silently drop or misattribute a spanner, so both raise an error instead of returning a wrong-but-silent plan.
